one_month_reasoning: Oct 31 is a Saturday, so the Oct 30 close counts. The main event in the window is 3Q26 earnings on Oct 28, which is also the last day of the FOMC meeting (Oct 27-28). Other items: the $0.50 dividend record date (Oct 27) [35] and the hyperscaler Q3 capex prints in late October. At Laguna (9/16) the CEO pre-signalled a 'very strong' 3Q order quarter and faster conversion of reservations to orders [17], so a strong orders headline is largely expected. He also said Electrification data-center orders drop to ~20% of segment orders in 2H, and that most of the 12 GW of new slots will be contracted in 4Q, not 3Q. EPS is the swing factor: consensus is ~$4.07-4.15 after the 2Q miss ($2.47 vs $3.04) [23]. New since round 1: Polymarket odds of an October hike fell from ~70% to 23% on Oct 1 after VC Jefferson signalled patience [32,34]. That lowers the chance of a hawkish shock on earnings day, but long yields stay high. The stock also already rebounded 3.9% on 10/1 [22]. I have no directional edge, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median ~$990 and monthly sigma ~15.5% (52%/3.5 plus a little for the earnings day). That gives P(>= spot) = 0.505.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, weighted 45/25/30, giving ~$983, roughly flat to spot. (1) P/E: Oct-2027 NTM EPS ~$29.6 x 34x = $1,006. (2) FCF yield: 2028 normalized FCF ~$8.4B (trimmed to sit with the >= $24B 2025-28 floor), i.e. $32.3/sh at 3.6%, plus $39.6/sh net cash = $937. (3) EV/EBITDA: 2028E $11.2B x 22x + $10.3B reported net cash, over 260M shares = $987.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus is $24.85-24.91 [4,26]; one aggregator shows $22.21. I lean low because of the 2Q EPS miss [23] and Erste's cuts.

Bottom-up from management's 2028 outlook [30]: $56B x 20% = $11.2B EBITDA, less ~$1.2-1.5B D&A, plus ~$0.3B interest income, ~20-21% tax, ~260M shares, gives ~$30.5-31.5. I trimmed my round-1 $32.0 back to $31.5. The supervisor noted that consensus revenue (~$61B) runs ahead of guidance, so the WallStreetZen $34.80 [26] gets less weight. Laguna's margin-in-backlog comments [17] keep me at the top of the bottom-up range.

The stock is ~41x 2027 consensus today. I compress the multiple as growth slows toward high-teens by late 2027. The 9/16 Fed hike [19] argues for a lower multiple. October hike odds dropping to 23% [32] partly offsets that, so I keep 34x. Anchors: Zaccardi ~40x [6] and GLJ ~17x [5].

methods.inputs: 2028 normalized FCF ~$8.4B / 260M shares = $32.3/sh at 3.6% = $897, plus $39.6/sh reported net cash ($10.3B)

inputs_detail.derivation: Verified in the 4Q25 release text. With 2025 at $3.7B and 2026 at ~$12B, the floor implies >= ~$8.3B for 2027-28 combined (supervisor finding, confirmed).

Cut from $9.1B. The >= $24B floor was set when 2026 FCF was guided at $5.0-5.5B [30]. Since then ~$6.5B has moved into 2026 [1], so 2027-28 FCF will be held down by the deposit unwind. I use ~75% conversion of $11.2B 2028E EBITDA, not 80%. I do not go lower, because the floor is conservative and the CEO says the progress-payment build is still smaller than the margin added to backlog [17].

Used consistently across all methods (fixes my round-1 inconsistency of $9.4B vs $12B). FCF through 2027 is assumed to fund buybacks and dividends, so net cash is held flat while the share count drifts to ~260M.
TTM FCF yield is ~4.7% on deposit-inflated FCF. 3.6% on normalized FCF is consistent with ~34x P/E in a higher-rate world.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion. Political friction (state moratoria, AI-slowdown calls, Oracle force majeure) delays data-center power projects, and a meaningful share of the 63 GW of reservations lapses instead of converting. The January 2027 margin-in-backlog disclosure disappoints, and the spring CMD's 2030 outlook underwhelms against Siemens and Mitsubishi capacity additions (GLJ case). FCF falls sharply in 2027 as deposits unwind. 2028 EPS ~$25-26 at ~23x NTM.

base.story: Backlog passes $200B early in 2027 and reservations keep converting. The January 2027 call delivers a 2027 outlook and a larger change in margin in backlog. The spring 2027 CMD sets a credible 2030 outlook, but the market already prices most of it. 2028 EPS of ~$30-32 is visible. FCF normalizes toward ~$8B as deposits unwind, and the multiple compresses from ~41x to ~34x NTM. The stock ends modestly above spot.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex runs to $1.3-1.4T in 2027 with no cuts. 2032 slots sell at premium pricing. The spring-2027 CMD lifts the 2028 targets and sets a strong 2030 outlook, with services as an annuity and Prolec ahead of plan. The market holds ~42x+ on ~$34 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$650 (about -34%), the market would be pricing ~21x on ~$31 2028E EPS, the multiple of a no-premium peer, or a cut to the 2028 outlook. That most likely means reservations are being cancelled or left unconverted (watch the 53 GW firm vs 63 GW reservation split at each quarter), margin in backlog has stalled (January 2027 disclosure), pricing on new slots has turned, or hyperscalers have actually cut capex. At 52% vol, ordinary swings rarely reach that level without fundamental news. I no longer cite the $560 buyback average as a floor: that is an 18-month programme average, and 1H26 purchases averaged $854 [1].

reasoning: Round 2 takes in the supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified where I could. (1) Net cash is $10.3B (cash $13.12B less borrowings $2.85B). I now use that one figure in every method, replacing $9.4B/$12B. (2) The >= $24B cumulative 2025-28 FCF floor is confirmed in the 4Q25 release text, alongside 2025 FCF of $3.7B and a 2026 guide that was then $5.0-5.5B. 2026 is now $11.5-12.5B, so the floor implies >= ~$8.3B for 2027-28 combined. I cut normalized 2028 FCF from $9.1B to $8.4B, and the FCF leg falls to $937. (3) The $560 buyback 'floor' was wrong. The 2Q26 release shows 1H26 buybacks averaged $854 (4.3M shares), with 2Q's ~2.5M shares at ~$920. Management buys near current prices, so I dropped the argument. (4) No December update: the guidance path is the January 2027 call, then a spring-2027 CMD with a 2030 outlook. That rerating event is still inside the 12-month horizon, so it shifts timing more than level. (5) The supervisor noted consensus revenue runs above guidance, so I trimmed 2028 EPS from $32 to $31.5. New lane evidence: Polymarket October-hike odds fell to 23% on 10/1 after Jefferson's remarks, which tempers my rate-driven multiple cut, so I hold 34x/22x/3.6% rather than cutting further. SemiAnalysis's analysis that 'cancelled' data-center capacity mostly lacks equipment orders supports the view that reservations reallocate rather than vanish. A search for slot-reservation cancellations found no new instance beyond Oracle's April switch to fuel cells. Result: fair value moves from $1,009 to $983 (~flat to spot). Scenario mean: 0.25x600 + 0.5x1030 + 0.25x1450 = $1,028. Its upside skew comes from the bull tail, not the fair value. Ladder: lognormal with median ~$990, sigma ~0.46, and a slightly fatter left tail for the deposit unwind, reservation and AI-politics risk. P(>= spot) = 0.505, down from 0.515. I disagree with the supervisor on the thesis break: I keep $650 rather than $640. The level is the same logic (~21x on ~$31 EPS), and the gap is immaterial. Limits: X/Reddit remained unreachable, and the Polymarket Fed market's volume was not visible in the fetched coverage.
